# Halatto: full product facts

> Vintage camera filter for iPhone: make photos you already took look shot on film, a disposable, instant, 90s or digital camera, with grain and a date stamp.

Companion to [llms.txt](https://halatto.app/llms.txt). Last updated: 2026-11-27.

## Product

- Name: Halatto (App Store title "Vintage Photo Filter – Halatto", subtitle "Film Grain & Old Camera Editor")
- Category: iOS app, App Store categories Graphics & Design and Utilities (vintage photo filter / film photo editor)
- Primary use case: make a photo you already have look like it was shot on film or an old camera (35mm, disposable, instant, toy camera, 90s point-and-shoot, Y2K digicam)
- Processing: on the iPhone, no account, nothing uploaded
- Publisher: Vladimir Ivakhnenko (c-basso)
- Website: https://halatto.app/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6758913511?pt=118672082&ct=web_en_llms_full&mt=8 (App Store id 6758913511)
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/halatto.app
- TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@halatto
- Pinterest: https://www.pinterest.com/halattoapp/

## Looks

14 looks in 5 groups. Each recreates a kind of camera, its film or sensor and its lens, not only a color grade.

- 35mm film: Tungsten 800 (Night cinema film. Red halos around lights, teal shadows); Titan 38 (Premium 90s compact. Crisp, cool shadows, warm highlights); Mju 35 (Pocket point-and-shoot in black and white. Hard contrast, big grain)
- Disposable: Snap 400 (Soft plastic lens, rainbow flare, greenish shadows); Snap Gold (Summer disposable. Golden, saturated, coarser grain)
- Instant: SX Fold (Folding instant. Glassy, deep blue shadows, lilac highlights); Square 600 (Boxy instant. Soft, green shadows, pink highlights); Mini Instant (Credit-card size. Clear, bright, a little cool)
- Toy camera: Tunnel 35 (Tunnel vignette, cross-processed color, a leak at the edge); Toy 120 (Medium-format toy. Dark corners, blur toward the edges); Dream 120 (Very soft, glowing highlights, a pink light leak)
- Y2K digicam: Silver IX (Warm silver compact. Pink skin, soft, purple fringing); Cyber Blue (Cool compact. Blue whites, contrast and noise); Digi 2MP (Early CCD. JPEG blocks, smeared color, streaks from lights)

## Tools

- Per look: strength, grain and film age
- Aging: fade, sunlight, yellowing, unevenness, dust, stains and creases; presets such as Shoebox and Faded print
- Light Leak: Edge, Window or Burn, in soft red, orange or golden
- Flash: Retro, Digital or Tanning, with intensity
- Date stamp: the orange film-camera date from the day the photo was taken; corner, direction, color and size
- Frame: puts the photo on a card, including instant cards (Instant, Mini, Wide)
- Crop, color and light adjustments
- Save as Recipe: keep an edit and apply it to other photos; Develop the Roll puts one look on many photos at once
- Before-and-after video export in Original, 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1
- Built-in camera with the look applied live; reopen an edit later; open a photo from the Photos share sheet

## Pricing and availability

- Free to download; every look and effect works up to a daily limit; a subscription or lifetime in-app purchase removes the limit
- iPhone only; requires iOS 18.6 or later; 89.3 MB download
- No Android version
- App localized in 31 languages
- On the App Store since November 2026

## Questions and answers

### How do I make my iPhone photos look like film?
Open the photo in Halatto, pick a film look such as Titan 38 or Tungsten 800, and raise grain and film age a little. Film color, grain and the softness of an old lens are what make a photo read as film; a color filter alone does not.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/make-photos-look-like-film-on-iphone/

### Is there a disposable camera filter for photos I already took?
Yes. Many disposable camera apps only work when you shoot in them. In Halatto you open any photo from your library and choose Snap 400 or Snap Gold, then add the flash and the orange date stamp.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/disposable-camera-filter-on-iphone/

### How do I get the Y2K digicam look on iPhone?
Pick one of the three digicam looks (Silver IX, Cyber Blue or Digi 2MP) and add the Digital flash. They add CCD color, sensor noise, cool whites and the hard flash of a 2000s compact camera.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/digicam-filter-y2k-photos-on-iphone/

### How do I add a date stamp to a photo on iPhone?
The Photos app cannot print a date on a picture. In Halatto open the photo, tap Date stamp and choose a corner: the orange date is taken from the day the photo was shot, and you can change its color, size and direction.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/add-date-stamp-to-photo-on-iphone/

### How can I make a photo look old?
Use Aging: start with the Shoebox or Faded print preset, then raise Fade and Yellowing and add dust, stains or creases. A warm film look and a light leak finish the effect.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/make-a-photo-look-old-on-iphone/

### Can I get a Polaroid-style instant photo look?
Yes. Halatto has three instant looks: SX Fold for the classic folding-camera color, Square 600 for the boxy instant look and Mini Instant for credit-card prints. Halatto is not affiliated with Polaroid or Fujifilm.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/instant-photo-effect-on-iphone/

### How do I add film grain to a photo on iPhone?
Every Halatto look has its own grain, and you can set the amount after you pick it. Grain looks most natural with a little fade and a softer lens, which the film looks add for you.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/add-film-grain-to-a-photo-on-iphone/

### How do I put the same filter on many photos at once?
Save your edit as a recipe, then use Develop the Roll: select the photos and tap Develop all to put the same camera on every one, so a trip looks like one roll of film.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/apply-the-same-filter-to-multiple-photos-on-iphone/

### Does Halatto upload my photos?
No. Photos are edited on your iPhone, there is no account, and nothing is uploaded to a server.
More: https://halatto.app/guides/best-vintage-camera-apps-for-iphone/#privacy

### Is Halatto free, and which devices does it run on?
It is free to download, and every look and effect works up to a daily limit. A subscription or a lifetime purchase removes the limit. It requires iOS 18.6 or later on iPhone; there is no Android version.
More: https://halatto.app/#faq

### Is there an Android version?
No. Halatto is published for iPhone on the Apple App Store only.

## Guides

### How to make your iPhone photos look like film
A photo reads as film when four things change together: film color (softer contrast, warm highlights, tinted shadows), grain, an old lens (softness, vignette, flare) and a little fade. The Photos app can only get you part of the way with Warmth, Contrast and Vignette. In Halatto, open the photo, pick a film look such as Titan 38 or Tungsten 800, raise grain and film age a little, and save. It works on photos you already took and edits on your iPhone.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/make-photos-look-like-film-on-iphone/

### Disposable camera filter for iPhone photos you already took
Many disposable camera apps only work when you shoot inside them. To put the look on a photo you already have, open it in Halatto and pick Snap 400 (soft plastic lens, rainbow flare, greenish shadows) or Snap Gold (golden, saturated, coarser grain). Add the Retro flash for indoor shots and the orange date stamp in the corner, then save.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/disposable-camera-filter-on-iphone/

### Digital camera filter: the old Y2K digicam look on iPhone
The Y2K digicam look comes from small CCD sensors and a hard built-in flash: punchy or cool color, digital noise, blown highlights and a slightly smeared, low-resolution JPEG. In Halatto, open the photo, pick Silver IX (warm, pink skin), Cyber Blue (blue whites, contrast) or Digi 2MP (early CCD with JPEG blocks and light streaks), then add the Digital flash.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/digicam-filter-y2k-photos-on-iphone/

### How to make a photo look old on iPhone
An old photo is faded, yellowed and physically worn. In Halatto, pick a warm film look first, then open Aging and start from the Shoebox or Faded print preset. Raise Fade and Yellowing, add some Unevenness, then dust, stains or creases and a light leak at the edge. The Photos app can only lower contrast and warm the color; it cannot add wear.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/make-a-photo-look-old-on-iphone/

### How to add a date stamp to a photo on iPhone, even one already taken
The iPhone Camera and Photos apps store the date in the photo's info but cannot print it on the picture. In Halatto, open the photo, tap Date stamp and pick a corner: the orange date is read from the day the photo was taken, in the '26 11 19 style of film cameras. Adjust Direction, Color and Size, then save.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/add-date-stamp-to-photo-on-iphone/

### Polaroid-style filter for iPhone: the instant photo look
Instant film has soft contrast, glassy or tinted shadows and pastel highlights. In Halatto pick SX Fold (folding instant: deep blue shadows, lilac highlights), Square 600 (boxy instant: green shadows, pink highlights) or Mini Instant (credit-card prints: clear, bright, a little cool), then crop to a square or portrait and add light aging. Halatto is not affiliated with Polaroid or Fujifilm.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/instant-photo-effect-on-iphone/

### How to add film grain to a photo on iPhone
The Photos app has no grain or noise slider. In Halatto, open the photo and pick any look: each film or camera has its own grain built in, and you can raise or lower the grain and film age after you pick it. For a modern photo with just texture, choose a subtle look like Mini Instant, lower its strength and raise grain.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/add-film-grain-to-a-photo-on-iphone/

### 90s photo filter: the point-and-shoot film look on iPhone
A 90s photo was usually shot on a 35mm compact or a disposable: crisp but slightly soft color, visible grain, a direct flash indoors and an orange date in the corner. In Halatto, choose Titan 38 (premium 90s compact), Mju 35 (pocket point-and-shoot in black and white) or Snap 400 (disposable), add the Retro flash for indoor shots and the date stamp, then save.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/90s-photo-filter-on-iphone/

### How to add a light leak effect to a photo on iPhone
A light leak is the warm glow from light that got onto the film by accident. In Halatto, open the photo, tap Light Leak, choose a preset (Soft red, Orange, Golden), pick the type (Edge for a glow from one side, Window for a soft patch, Burn for a strong blown-out flare), then set Color, Amount and Position. Or pick a toy camera look, such as Tunnel 35 or Dream 120, that already leaks.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/add-light-leaks-to-a-photo-on-iphone/

### How to apply the same filter to multiple photos on iPhone
In Photos, edit one photo, tap the More button and choose Copy Edits, then select the other photos, tap More and Paste Edits. That copies Photos adjustments only. For a film look on a whole set, edit one photo in Halatto and Save as Recipe, or open Develop the Roll, choose a camera, select the photos and tap Develop all.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/apply-the-same-filter-to-multiple-photos-on-iphone/

### Best vintage and film camera apps for iPhone
Pick by how you work. If you want to shoot with the look on and enjoy a disposable-style ritual, a camera-first app like Huji Cam, Dazz Cam or Dispo fits. If you want deep film color grading, VSCO or RNI Films. If you want to turn photos you already took into film or old-camera shots, with aging, light leaks, a date stamp and batch editing, use an editor like Halatto.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/best-vintage-camera-apps-for-iphone/

### How to make a before and after photo video on iPhone
After you edit a photo in Halatto, open Export and choose the video option: a divider sweeps across the photo from the original to the film look. Pick Original, 9:16 (Stories, Reels, TikTok), 4:5 (feed) or 1:1, and tap Share video. Doing the same in a video editor means exporting two images and animating a mask by hand.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/make-a-before-and-after-photo-video-on-iphone/

### Halation effect: what it is and how to get the film glow on iPhone
Halation is the red-orange glow around bright lights on film without an anti-halation layer, made famous by tungsten-balanced cinema film used for stills. iPhone photos never show it. In Halatto, open a night photo with lights in the frame and pick Tungsten 800: red halos around lights, teal shadows and film grain. Lower the strength for skin, raise grain for a grittier frame.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/night-film-halation-glow-on-iphone/

### Apps like Dazz Cam for iPhone, for photos you already took
Dazz Cam is built around shooting: you pick a simulated camera and take a new photo. If you mostly shoot new photos, Dazz and apps like Huji or NOMO CAM fit. If you want the same old-camera look on photos already in your library, with aging, light leaks, a date stamp and one look on a whole set, use an editor such as Halatto.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/apps-like-dazz-cam-for-iphone/

### How to make iPhone photos look like film without an app
Open the photo in Photos, tap Edit, then Adjust. For a film look, lower Contrast and Highlights, raise Warmth, add a little Vignette and lower Saturation slightly. Below are starting values for three looks. Photos cannot add grain, light leaks or lens softness, so the result is a warm, soft photo rather than a true film print.
Guide: https://halatto.app/guides/make-iphone-photos-look-like-film-without-an-app/
